title: Introduce telemetry fanout optimizer and token-slot attribution
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: our current telemetry fanout duplicates token-level metrics across many downstream consumers which increases ingestion cost and causes noisy long-tail cardinality. This PR implements a fanout optimizer that deduplicates and buckets token emission by 'token-slot' (a lightweight shape fingerprint) and provides a deterministic attribution map so dashboards and SLOs can show per-slot cost/latency breakdowns.

This is a single continuous description but includes: design, testing, rollout, and operational notes. Design summary: 1) Introduce a telemetry fanout optimizer (server-side component) that tracks active downstream consumers and merges redundant metric emissions when semantics permit. 2) Add a token-slot attribution layer that computes a compact 8-bit slot id per invocation prefix+model-shape and attaches it as telemetry.token_slot. 3) Expose a new set of aggregated dashboards (token-slot heatmap, slot-cost waterfall) and a lightweight query-time mapping so users can drill from slot->invocations. 4) Provide runtime config with per-route fanout tolerances and fallthrough rules to preserve critical tracing for SLO-sensitive flows.

Compatibility and safety: optimizer is opt-in per-tenant by default. For tenants with strict fidelity (enterprise tier) the feature defaults to pass-through. The token-slot is purely additive metadata and is separate from any PII or prompt content; hashing is salted per-tenant and non-reversible.

Testing: unit tests for optimizer logic and slot assignment (observability/fanout/optimizer_test.go), e2e against a reduced fanout topology using ci/test/telemetry-e2e.yaml, and a small synthetic replay harness to verify no statistical bias in SLO calculations.

Rollout plan: feature flag rollout across a canary cohort (5% of traffic) -> 25% -> 100% with metrics to monitor (slot cardinality, downstream ingestion delta, alert noise). If slot-cardinality grows > 2x expected baseline for a tenant, automatically revert for that tenant.

Related work: references Linear ENG-4201 (fanout-cost reduction) and ENG-4270 (token-cost decomposition). Also complements dashboards added in PRs that introduced token heatmaps; this PR adds attribution to make those panels actionable.

Checklist: - [x] Core optimizer implementation - [x] Token-slot assignment and hashing - [x] Unit tests and integration tests - [x] Dashboard JSON for Console - [x] Docs/playbook describing operational signals - [x] Linear links and instrumentation for rollback

CI summary: all checks green on final run (lint, unit, integration with local telemetry harness).

Merge notes: squash-merged into main. See release notes field for customer-facing blurb.

release_notes: Add a telemetry fanout optimizer that reduces redundant downstream metric emissions and a token-slot attribution field to enable compact per-slot cost and latency breakdowns. Opt-in by default and gated by tenant config. Includes new dashboards: Token-Slot Heatmap and Slot-Cost Waterfall. Monitoring: fanout_reduction_ratio, slot_cardinality_by_tenant.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report missing high-fidelity traces after rollout, check tenant config flags (pkg/config/fanout.yaml) and the per-tenant rollback log at /var/log/redwood/telemetry_fanout_reverts.log. Key signals: sudden spike in slot_cardinality, downstream consumer 429s, or increase in SLO alert rate after reduction. Revert by toggling tenant.flag.telemetry_fanout=false.
